cond_0001.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research.
At least two (2) years of experience participating in data science and analytics related projects or research.
Relevant programming and data management experience, including experience with R, SQL, and Python.
Strong programming/analytical background.
Preferred Requirements
Proficiency in the field of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive familiarity with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.
Experience with Microsoft applications and tools, including in-depth technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.
Experience in any of the following areas: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, is looking for data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
cond_0042.responsibilities:
Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The role calls for regular engagement with a multi-disciplinary team and involves staying in close contact with colleagues across child development, clinical research, statistics, and software development. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
This position involves:
Developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development, working closely with team members to clarify requirements and walk collaborators through findings.
Adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking, including actively contributing to discussions on methodology and raising issues early.
Advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes, connecting regularly with Dr. Shic and the broader team to align on priorities.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
cond_0042.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research.
At least two (2) years of experience participating in data science and analytics related projects or research.
Relevant programming and data management experience, including experience with R, SQL, and Python.
Strong programming/analytical background.
Preferred Requirements
Proficiency in the field of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive familiarity with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.
Experience with Microsoft applications and tools, including in-depth technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.

cond_0063.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, is seeking data scientists to help advance next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary areas of this work are: (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental and cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research, and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming and software development. This position involves: (1) collaborating on mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) working alongside the team on adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) contributing to additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. A strong programming and analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
cond_0063.responsibilities: Work alongside the team under limited technical direction to help develop data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. This role requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
cond_0063.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research.
At least two (2) years of experience participating in data science and analytics related projects or research.
Relevant programming and data management experience, including experience with R, SQL, and Python.
Experience with Microsoft applications and tools, including in-depth technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.
Preferred Requirements
Proficiency in the field of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive familiarity with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.

cond_0074.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development. This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
Our research offices are located in [Location masked]. We are affiliated with the Center for Child Health, Behavior and Development at [Company name masked], the [Company name masked] Autism Center, and Departments of Pediatrics, Computer Science & Engineering, and Psychology at the University of Washington.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.

cond_0163.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development.
cond_0163.responsibilities:
Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.

cond_0186.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, is looking for data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
cond_0186.responsibilities:
Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The role calls for regular engagement with a multi-disciplinary team and involves staying in close contact with colleagues across child development, clinical research, statistics, and software development. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
This position involves:
Developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development, working closely with team members to clarify requirements and walk collaborators through findings.
Adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking, including actively contributing to discussions on methodology and raising issues early.
Advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes, connecting regularly with Dr. Shic and the broader team to align on priorities.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.

cond_0222.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, is looking for data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
cond_0222.responsibilities:
Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The role calls for regular engagement with a multi-disciplinary team and involves staying in close contact with colleagues across child development, clinical research, statistics, and software development. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
This position involves:
Developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development, working closely with team members to clarify requirements and walk collaborators through findings.
Adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking, including actively contributing to discussions on methodology and raising issues early.
Advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes, connecting regularly with Dr. Shic and the broader team to align on priorities.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
cond_0222.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research.
At least two (2) years of experience participating in data science and analytics related projects or research.
Relevant programming and data management experience, including experience with R, SQL, and Python.
Strong programming/analytical background.
Preferred Requirements
Proficiency in the field of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive familiarity with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.
Experience with Microsoft applications and tools, including in-depth technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.

cond_0232.intro:
We are looking for a Data Scientist I to join our team.
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, is seeking a data scientist to support next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary focus areas are: (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental and cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will report directly to Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research, and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team with backgrounds in child development, clinical research, statistics, and software development.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. A strong programming and analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
Our research offices are located at [Location masked]. We are affiliated with the Center for Child Health, Behavior and Development at [Company name masked], the [Company name masked] Autism Center, and Departments of Pediatrics, Computer Science & Engineering, and Psychology at the University of Washington.
cond_0232.responsibilities:
Work under limited technical direction on the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
Develop mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention measures to child development outcomes.
Adapt and evaluate eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based approaches.
Contribute to additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes, coordinating with team members on specific deliverables as required.
cond_0232.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research.
At least two (2) years of experience participating in data science and analytics related projects or research.
Proficiency in the field of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive familiarity with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.
Experience with Microsoft applications and tools, including in-depth technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.
Relevant programming and data management experience, including experience with R, SQL, and Python.

cond_0374.intro:
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development. This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
Our research offices are located in [Location masked]. We are affiliated with the Center for Child Health, Behavior and Development at [Company name masked], the [Company name masked] Autism Center, and Departments of Pediatrics, Computer Science & Engineering, and Psychology at the University of Washington.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with eye tracking, data analysis, and applied research in child development.

[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development. This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
Our research offices are located in [Location masked]. We are affiliated with the Center for Child Health, Behavior and Development at [Company name masked], the [Company name masked] Autism Center, and Departments of Pediatrics, Computer Science & Engineering, and Psychology at the University of Washington.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
cond_0434.responsibilities: Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. The position requires skills in data science, statistics, and computer science, particularly as they apply to the analysis and management of complex biomedical and clinical data.
cond_0434.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 2 years of demonstrated expertise in data science and analytics projects or research.
Proven track record in relevant programming and data management, with deep knowledge of R, SQL, and Python.
Preferred Requirements
Advanced knowledge of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive expertise with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.
Strong command of Microsoft applications and tools, with substantial technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.

cond_0445.intro:
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development. This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of AI/ML approaches applied to developmental and clinical data.

cond_0500.intro:
[Company name masked] Innovative Technologies Lab, led by Dr. Frederick Shic, seeks data scientists interested in advancing next-generation technologies (mobile applications, emphasizing remote eye tracking) that assess and predict infant development. The primary emphases of this work are on (1) AI/ML-driven characterization of developmental/cognitive abilities in infants; and (2) robust prediction of developmental outcomes, especially as related to autism spectrum conditions. Additional areas of focus include: biomarker discovery and refinement; human-centered design; eye-tracking methods; and behavioral imaging through computer vision.
The data scientist will work directly with Dr. Frederick Shic, a computer scientist by training with primary expertise in eye tracking, early development, and autism research; and will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team experienced with child development, clinical research, statistics, and computer programming/software development. This position involves (1) developing mobile app-based systems and methods that link attention to child development; (2) adaptation and evaluation of eye-tracking methods, with a focus on comparing webcam-based versus laboratory-based eye tracking; and (3) advancement of additional research topics relevant to predicting child outcomes.
Experience in any of the following areas is of interest: Mobile Device Development/Applications, Computer Vision, Human-Centered Design, Visualization, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Probabilistic Modeling, Statistics, Computer Science, and Optimization. Strong programming/analytical background is necessary for all candidates.
Our research offices are located in [Location masked]. We are affiliated with the Center for Child Health, Behavior and Development at [Company name masked], the [Company name masked] Autism Center, and Departments of Pediatrics, Computer Science & Engineering, and Psychology at the University of Washington.
For more information, please see our website or contact Dr. Shic directly at fshic@uw.edu.
People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with eye tracking, data analysis, and applied research in child development.
cond_0500.responsibilities: Work under limited technical direction in the development of data analysis and management tools for specialized data and analytics projects. cond_0500.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or comparable area of research.
At least two (2) years of experience participating in data science and analytics related projects or research.
Proficiency in the field of Biomedical/Health Informatics, including extensive familiarity with biological data, molecular biological databases, and clinical databases.
Experience with Microsoft applications and tools, including in-depth technical and/or applications knowledge in assigned platforms.
Relevant programming and data management experience, including experience with R, SQL, and Python.
